You are a joinery drafting reference. Answer only from the supplied workshop reference material, and cite the file and section you used.
How do I draw the door reveal on an elevation?

A 2-3 mm reveal between door edges and between door and carcass. Draw it as two parallel lines on the visible layer at 0.25 mm, measured from the actual door edge (never from the finished veneer face). Keep it at 2 mm in wet areas so swelling board cannot bind.

Source: references/joinery-practice.md › Doors; data/rules.yaml › doors.gap_min/gap_max
You are a joinery drafting reference. Answer only from the supplied workshop reference material, and cite the file and section you used.
Where do dimensions go — carcass face or finished face?

Dimensions always go to the carcass face, never to the veneer or paint. Veneer (0.6 mm) and paint (0.3 mm) are drawn as separate layers in a detail, but the dimension chain stays closed on the carcass so error does not accumulate across adjacent units.

Source: data/rules.yaml › drafting.dimension_reference
You are a joinery drafting reference. Answer only from the supplied workshop reference material, and cite the file and section you used.
What scale and line weights for a carcass detail?

Construction detail 1:5, unit section 1:10, fixing detail 1:2. Line weights: cut 0.50 mm, visible 0.25 mm, hidden 0.13 mm dashed, dimensions 0.13 mm. Hatch along the grain, and draw the veneer as its own 0.6 mm layer on the board face.

Source: data/rules.yaml › drafting.scale and drafting.lineweights_mm
You are a joinery drafting reference. Answer only from the supplied workshop reference material, and cite the file and section you used.
Can I use a 25 mm board for a carcass?

Only if the shop stocks it. Where boards come in 8 and 18 mm, build the thickness up in layers (18+8+18 = 44 mm, 18+18+18 = 54 mm) and show the build-up in a detail. Never call for a size nobody sells.

Source: data/rules.yaml › stock_sizes; panel_thickness
You are a joinery drafting reference. Answer only from the supplied workshop reference material, and cite the file and section you used.
How much gap do I leave between joinery and the ceiling?

At least 20 mm, always. Joinery never runs tight to the ceiling: ceiling movement and site levels will either crack it or bind it. Stop the unit 20 mm below the soffit and keep an even shadow gap; model the real gap, not a rounded dimension.

Source: data/rules.yaml › shadow_gap.to_ceiling_min
You are a joinery drafting reference. Answer only from the supplied workshop reference material, and cite the file and section you used.
What goes in the hinge detail?

A 35 mm cup set 22.5 mm from the door edge (centre of cup), an 8 mm press-in dowel for the cup, and mounting plates on 5x12 mm plastic dowels — never a screw straight into board. Every unit with doors carries the detail, and the hardware table counts items by number, not by area.

Source: data/rules.yaml › doors.hinge_cup_diameter / hinge_dowel_mm / plate_dowel_mm
You write clean AutoLISP for AutoCAD. Draw on the layers A-CUT / A-VISIBLE / A-DIM / A-TEXT only, dimensioned in millimetres.
Write AutoLISP that draws the front elevation of a 600x720 base unit with a 150 plinth.

(defun c:BASE-ELEV ( / w h p t)
  (setq w 600.0 h 720.0 p 150.0 t 18.0)
  (setvar "OSMODE" 0)
  (command "_.LAYER" "_M" "A-CUT" "_C" 7 "" "_LW" 0.50 "A-CUT" "")
  (command "_.LAYER" "_M" "A-VISIBLE" "_C" 7 "" "_LW" 0.25 "A-VISIBLE" "")
  (command "_.RECTANG" (list 0.0 p) (list w (+ p h)))
  (command "_.RECTANG" (list 2.0 (+ p 2.0)) (list (- w 2.0) (- (+ p h) 2.0)))
  (princ "\nelevation drawn on A-CUT / A-VISIBLE")
  (princ))
You write clean AutoLISP for AutoCAD. Draw on the layers A-CUT / A-VISIBLE / A-DIM / A-TEXT only, dimensioned in millimetres.
AutoLISP to draw a 1600x2400 wardrobe outline with a centre partition.

(defun c:WARDROBE ( / w h t xc)
  (setq w 1600.0 h 2400.0 t 18.0 xc (/ w 2.0))
  (setvar "OSMODE" 0)
  (command "_.RECTANG" (list 0.0 0.0) (list w h))
  (command "_.LINE" (list (- xc (/ t 2.0)) 0.0) (list (- xc (/ t 2.0)) h) "")
  (command "_.LINE" (list (+ xc (/ t 2.0)) 0.0) (list (+ xc (/ t 2.0)) h) "")
  (princ))
